strategies.name: Sequential all-reduce with interleaved local ops
strategies.desc: Performs 8 all-reduce calls with local scale/unscale operations between each, as shown in the reference. 8 collective dispatches total. Straightforward but maximizes dispatch overhead; no overlap or fusion opportunities exploited.

strategies.name: Fused scale computation with bulk all-reduce
strategies.desc: Precompute all scaling coefficients as tensors, then perform element-wise multiplications in bulk before each all-reduce to enable operator fusion. Still 8 all-reduce dispatches but reduces local compute dispatches from ~24 (8×3 clone/scale/unscale) to ~16 by fusing scale operations into single vectorized ops per stage.

strategies.name: Tensor concatenation with single large all-reduce
strategies.desc: Stack/concatenate intermediate buffers across all 8 stages into a single large tensor (world*256*8), apply all local transformations as strided views/slices, then issue one giant all-reduce. Reduces to 1 collective dispatch at cost of 8× memory and larger single payload; trades dispatch overhead for bandwidth.

strategies.name: Pipelined reduce-scatter then all-gather pattern
strategies.desc: Decompose each all-reduce into reduce-scatter followed by all-gather (16 total collectives). Allows pipelining where reduce-scatter of stage i+1 overlaps with all-gather of stage i. Total 16 dispatches but with potential overlap; exploits bandwidth-compute hiding at cost of doubled collective count.

strategies.name: Hierarchical reduction with broadcast fanout
strategies.desc:
Replace all-reduce with reduce (to rank 0) + broadcast pattern for each stage, enabling rank 0 to batch-compute all 8 stage transformations before broadcasting final result. Reduces to 8 reduce + 1 broadcast = 9 dispatches, but creates bottleneck at rank 0 and increases latency due to tree depth.
